counterevidence_considered.description: The procedure used is of the row-independent type that this issue class targets: Fisher's exact test applied to rows treated as independent Bernoulli outcomes. This makes the analysis susceptible in principle if a unit were duplicated, but inspection of the data and code shows no duplication occurred, so this precondition alone does not demonstrate the issue.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: row-independent procedure present; no duplicated unit found

source_refs.quoted_text:
Each row of `data/input.csv` is one restored dune slack, walked once during the
2025 flowering season. No slack contributes more than one row, so the 24 rows
are 24 independent units and a row-independent test is appropriate.

evidence.description: The input data contain exactly 24 data rows and 24 distinct site_id values (DS01 through DS24), each appearing on exactly one row, so no independent unit enters the cross-tabulation more than once. Verified by listing all site codes from line 2 through line 25 of the CSV.

The workflow code explicitly enforces one row per independent unit: it raises a hard error if any site_id appears on more than one row before any statistics are computed, so a duplicated unit could not silently reach the Fisher test.
The data description states each slack was surveyed and entered exactly once, ruling out repeated-measures structure hidden behind single rows, and confirms site_id values are unique.
evidence.observed_value: one survey per slack; site_id unique per row

evidence.description: Independent recomputation of the 2x2 table from the raw CSV gives inversion 9 present / 3 absent and stripping 3 present / 9 absent, odds ratio 9.00, and two-sided Fisher exact p = 2*(52901/2704156) = 0.0391, exactly matching the report; the reported result is therefore reproduced from unduplicated per-site rows.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by (1) checking every site_id in data/input.csv for repeats: DS01-DS24 each appear exactly once across the 24 data rows; (2) looking for near-duplicate covariate rows (same method/area/age) that could indicate a re-entered site under a different code: all area values are distinct; (3) tracing the code path for any aggregation, merge, resampling, or loop that could feed a row into the 2x2 table more than once: cross_tabulate increments exactly one cell per row and read_slacks raises on duplicated codes; (4) recomputing the table, odds ratio (9.00), and two-sided Fisher p-value (0.0391) from the raw CSV, which matched the report exactly, confirming the reported result derives from one entry per independent unit. All attempts to exhibit a repeated independent-unit entry failed.
